assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pd-catalyzed C-N cross-coupling turned aryl amination from a forcing, substrate-limited process into a routine bond construction. Ligand design (bulky biaryl phosphines, chelating and hindered alkylphosphines) gave broad scope, and the method is ubiquitous in medicinal and process chemistry and total synthesis. It is exactly the kind of general method that changed how chemists everywhere build bonds, and it extends the logic honored in 2010 for C-C coupling.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig independently developed the catalytic, ligand-controlled, general version and the mechanistic understanding of amine coordination, deprotonation and reductive elimination. Kosugi's earlier tin-amide coupling was a precursor needing stoichiometric tin reagents; a two-person prize is cleanest, acknowledging that Kosugi's precedent is a historical footnote I cannot fully weigh.
assessment.maturity: Mature: more than two decades of independent use, adoption in industry at scale, and a stable mechanistic picture. Recognition is, if anything, overdue.
uncertainties: Whether the committee wants a third laureate for the Kosugi precursor; I am relying on recalled literature history rather than verified priority claims.
Possible overlap with the 2010 Pd cross-coupling prize may make some members reluctant.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Visible-light photoredox catalysis created a mild, general way to generate radicals and radical ions with simple light sources and transition-metal or organic photocatalysts, opening transformations that were hard by two-electron chemistry. It has been broadly adopted in methodology, late-stage functionalization and industrial settings, and it reshaped how many synthesis groups think about reactivity.
assessment.attribution: Credit is diffuse. Yoon, Stephenson and MacMillan in 2008-2009 independently showed synthetic photoredox, Nicewicz extended it to organic photocatalysts and arene C-H functionalization, and König and Fukuzumi have earlier precedent. MacMillan is already a 2021 laureate, so I propose three others; the allocation is genuinely contested.
assessment.maturity: Strong and independent confirmation and very wide use; the field is still evolving, but the core concept is stable. Timing is reasonable, though some applications are still being scaled.
uncertainties: Attribution is disputed among several groups with overlapping early contributions and precursors in earlier photochemistry.
MacMillan's earlier prize may influence how the committee weighs the field; I cannot verify committee precedent.
Reproducibility and mechanistic claims in some photoredox reports remain debated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Selective C-H functionalization lets chemists treat C-H bonds as functional groups, shortening syntheses and enabling late-stage diversification. Directing-group, ligand-accelerated and template strategies for site selectivity, including remote positions, are a conceptual advance with wide use in medicinal chemistry and natural product synthesis. This speaks directly to efficiency in synthesis.
assessment.attribution: Yu's ligand-enabled Pd(II) catalysis and template-based distal selectivity and Sanford's Pd(II)/Pd(IV) catalysis and directed functionalization are the most decisive contributions. Daugulis, Hartwig and Smith made important parallel contributions (e.g. directing groups, borylation) so allocation is hard and some excellent contributors are left out.
assessment.maturity: Highly active field with many independent confirmations and growing industrial uptake, but still maturing, with scope limits for unactivated and sp3 sites. Slightly early compared with C-N coupling.
uncertainties: Breadth of the field makes a clean 'one discovery' formulation difficult.
Industrial use is less routine than for cross-coupling; I am relying on recalled literature rather than checked usage statistics.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Isolation of stable carbenes (imidazolylidenes, and Bertrand's phosphino-carbenes and later cyclic alkyl amino carbenes) overturned the view that carbenes are only transient and gave a new class of ligands and organocatalysts. NHC-ligated metals underpin modern olefin metathesis catalysts, cross-coupling and organocatalysis, so the practical effect on synthesis is large.
assessment.attribution: Arduengo isolated the first crystalline NHC in 1991 and Bertrand reported the first stable carbene in 1988; these are the clear conceptual originators. Nolan, Rovis and Bode made major downstream applications that I regard as application rather than the core discovery.
assessment.maturity: Over thirty years of confirmation and wide use; the recognition is mature. Possible concern is that applications have been partly honored through the 2005 metathesis prize.
uncertainties: Whether the 1988 Bertrand compound and the 1991 Arduengo compound are weighted equally as the original discovery.
Overlap with the metathesis prize may affect appetite; unverified committee view.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Frustrated Lewis pairs show that sterically hindered Lewis acid-base pairs can heterolytically activate H2 and other small molecules without a metal, giving metal-free hydrogenation and a new concept in reactivity. It is chemically new, simple to state and has influenced main-group catalysis.
assessment.attribution: Stephan's 2006 metal-free reversible H2 activation and subsequent catalytic hydrogenations, and Erker's work on intramolecular and reactivity of FLPs, are the main contributions. Fair as a two-person configuration; Stephan's contribution is the more decisive.
assessment.maturity: Over fifteen years of confirmation, though the scale of practical application remains modest compared with transition-metal catalysis. Somewhat early on impact, mature on concept.
uncertainties: Practical impact in industry and synthesis is still limited.
Some mechanistic interpretations (single-electron pathways) are debated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Bergman's intermolecular oxidative addition of unreactive alkane C-H bonds to Ir(I) in 1982 was a landmark showing that saturated hydrocarbons can be cleaved under mild homogeneous conditions. It created the mechanistic foundation for later C-H functionalization and is conceptually very clean.
assessment.attribution: Single credited name, though Graham, Jones and Periana made closely related and sometimes simultaneous contributions that are not among the credited names here, so the single-laureate framing is fair only within this candidate's supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Very mature and extensively confirmed mechanistically, but catalytic applications remain modest, and Bergman might be viewed as foundational rather than a practical breakthrough. Recognition could be viewed as late.
uncertainties: Practical synthetic use of the original stoichiometric reaction is limited.
Contributions by others at the time (Graham) cannot be properly credited with this list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native chemical ligation allows chemoselective joining of unprotected peptide fragments in water, making total chemical synthesis and semisynthesis of proteins routine. It is a new way to build large complex molecules and has been used for modified proteins, including in therapeutic and research settings.
assessment.attribution: Dawson and Kent reported the 1994 NCL, with Kent's group developing it further for protein synthesis; Muir's expressed protein ligation extended it to semisynthesis. Danishefsky contributed major methodology and synthetic applications, so some contributors would be left out.
assessment.maturity: Three decades of independent use and stable chemistry; mature and timely. Competes with biology-leaning candidates, and the border-field question is what was chemically new, which here is clearly the chemoselective ligation.
uncertainties: Allocation among Dawson, Kent, Muir and Danishefsky is contested.
Scale limits for very large proteins and competition from recombinant expression temper the impact.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Atom transfer radical polymerization gave controlled radical polymerization with predictable molecular weight, narrow dispersity and complex architectures from many monomers under practical conditions. It has had wide use in polymer materials and is an example of a method adopted broadly.
assessment.attribution: Matyjaszewski and Sawamoto reported the transition-metal-mediated living radical polymerization in 1995, independently. Wang and Matyjaszewski are credited with the first ATRP report and Kamigaito is a collaborator of Sawamoto; I choose the two clear senior leaders, but the exact division is uncertain.
assessment.maturity: Mature, widely used, and independently confirmed. Competes with RAFT and nitroxide-mediated polymerization, and the question of which controlled-radical method deserves recognition is unresolved.
uncertainties: Credit allocation between Matyjaszewski/Wang and Sawamoto/Kamigaito is uncertain.
Whether the committee would prefer to honor controlled radical polymerization as a whole, including RAFT.
